stories.headline: King Harald V of Norway dies at 89 as son Haakon VIII ascends throne
stories.body: King Harald V of Norway died on August 28 at the age of 89. He ruled Norway for 35 years. His 53-year-old son immediately became the new monarch as King Haakon VIII. Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store said that an era has ended and a new one begins. Store added that the king is dead and long live the king. King Harald V stayed in an Oslo hospital from August 17. He suffered from haemolytic anaemia. The Norwegian Armed Forces honoured the late king with a 21-shot funeral salute. They fired the salute from Akershus Fortress in central Oslo. King Haakon VIII's 22-year-old daughter Ingrid Alexandra became the new crown princess and next in line to the throne. Britain's King Charles III paid tribute to King Harald V. King Charles III called him a towering figure who guided Norway with warmth and humility. Public support for the monarchy in Norway dropped to 54% in February from 72% in 2024. In June, Crown Princess Mette-Marit's son, Marius Borg Hoiby, received a four-year prison sentence after a rape conviction.

stories.headline: US announces deal with Venezuela securing majority control of oil reserves
stories.body: US President Donald Trump announced an agreement with Venezuela to secure American control over massive oil reserves. The deal covers more than 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves in Venezuela. A US official said that the US government will retain 55% effective control of a joint venture under the deal. That joint venture includes a private operator. The private operator was granted a 100-year concession in Venezuela. Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez said the agreement involves developing 17 strategic oil fields. Rodriguez said the project will draw over $100 billion in investment. She added that the operation will generate over $209 billion in state taxes. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the Venezuela oil deal will bring nearly $100 billion in private investment. Rubio said the project will support thousands of high-paying jobs. The agreement comes after political changes in South America. On January 3, US special forces captured former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro. US special forces also captured his wife, Cilia Flores, on that day. In early August, the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve dropped below 300 million barrels. The reserve has decreased by over 100 million barrels since early 2026. On August 28, the average price of petrol in the United States reached $4.09 a gallon. That price compares to $3.21 a gallon recorded one year earlier.

stories.headline: Israel kills three Palestinian fighters in West Bank drone strike
stories.body: Israel killed three Palestinians in a drone strike in the West Bank town of Jenin. The attack was the first Israeli military air strike in the West Bank since February 2025. The Israeli military said it eliminated three militants during the strike. Military officials identified one of the dead men as Hamas operative Qais Bitawi. Palestinian Islamic Jihad said that Qais Bitawi and two other men killed in Jenin were its fighters. Palestinian Islamic Jihad identified Bitawi as a leader in the Al-Quds Brigades. The Palestinian Red Crescent said Israeli forces briefly detained its medical crews at the strike site. The organization said Israeli forces confiscated its equipment. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz posted on social media about the operation. Katz posted on X that the strike shows the fruits of an aggressive policy in the West Bank. Katz wrote that Israel does not wait for terror, but pursues it, conquers its strongholds, and thwarts its people.

stories.headline: Meta agrees to $18 billion settlement and new youth safety rules
stories.body: Meta agreed to an $18 billion settlement with US states and territories. The agreement ends a federal lawsuit alleging that Meta's social media platforms harmed children's mental health. Meta agreed to implement a combined default daily screen-time limit of two hours across Facebook and Instagram for minor accounts. Meta will introduce an automatic night mode blocking minor profiles from Feeds, Stories, Reels, and Explore pages between midnight and 6:00 am. Meta's new School Mode will default to muting standard push notifications for teenage users between 8:00 am and 3:00 pm. Meta announced it will withhold $5 billion of its $18 billion settlement. Meta will withhold the funds until rival platforms like TikTok and YouTube enter into similar youth protection agreements.

stories.headline: Greenland creates truth commission to examine historic forced contraception campaign
stories.body: Greenland announced the creation of a Truth and Reconciliation Commission to examine a historical forced contraception campaign. The commission will examine actions taken against Indigenous Inuit women and girls. A joint inquiry revealed that between the 1960s and 1990s, at least 4,000 Greenlandic Inuits were fitted with IUDs or received contraceptive injections without informed consent. By the late 1970s, at least 4,070 women had been fitted with an IUD. That figure represented one out of every two Greenlandic women of childbearing age. The Danish parliament approved compensation payments of up to 300,000 Danish crowns, or $46,758, for each affected woman. A four-member expert panel appointed to investigate the campaign split and submitted two conflicting reports on whether the actions constituted genocide. Panel experts Dalee Sambo Dorough and Miriam Cullen determined that Inuit women's rights were violated. However, they said they could not conclude genocide occurred based on contraceptive practices alone.

stories.headline: Nepal and China report nearly 600 deaths after flash floods hit region
stories.body: Nepal and Chinese authorities reported nearly 600 flood deaths after a glacier collapsed on Wednesday,. The glacier collapse triggered flash floods across Nepal and Tibet, leaving over 2,400 people missing. Nepal's official death toll reached 579, while Chinese state media reported seven deaths in Tibet. Authorities reported at least 2,478 people missing after the flood. That total included 1,924 missing in Nepal and 554 missing in Tibet. More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal. The Red Cross said at least 93,000 people were affected by the disaster. Chinese authorities evacuated 555 stranded tourists and 499 Chinese residents from Tibet. Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said Nepal needs foreign technical assistance for specialized tasks. Khanal mentioned tunnel rescue, body identification, DNA testing, and body storage. Nepal Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle said Nepal will require at least a few billion dollars to recover from the flood destruction. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah shortly after the disaster to offer humanitarian assistance. India sent 62 tonnes of emergency relief assistance to Nepal across three airlifts. The United Arab Emirates allocated $10 million in humanitarian aid to Nepal through the UAE Aid Agency. Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar received 21 pilgrims from Tamil Nadu who were rescued from flood areas in Nepal. At least 320 Indian nationals remained uncontactable in Nepal. Official sources said 149 Indian nationals crossed over from China into Nepal on August 28, 2026.

stories.headline: Karnataka Minister B. Nagendra resigns following financial irregularity allegations
stories.body: Karnataka Minister B. Nagendra submitted his resignation on Friday. His resignation came 25 days after he was re-inducted into the state cabinet. Nagendra faces opposition allegations regarding the alleged misappropriation of ₹89 crore from the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation. Nagendra requested permission from Congress leadership to resign as a member of the legislative assembly in addition to stepping down from his cabinet position. Announcing his decision, Nagendra said that he was voluntarily tendering his resignation as minister. Financial irregularities in the corporation surfaced in May 2024 after an accounts superintendent died by suicide and left a note alleging unauthorized fund transfers. Nagendra had previously resigned as tribal welfare minister in June 2024. He was re-inducted into the cabinet on August 3 after D.K. Shivakumar became Chief Minister. Protests by opposition parties over Nagendra's return led to the Karnataka Legislature's monsoon session being adjourned on August 24. Police took BJP leaders B.Y. Vijayendra and R. Ashoka into preventive custody during a protest march toward the Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru.

stories.headline: Indian food authority proposes red warning labels on packaged food high in fat and sugar
stories.body: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India proposed red hexagonal warning labels on packaged foods. The agency filed a compliance affidavit with the Supreme Court detailing the proposal. The case stems from a public interest lawsuit filed by the NGO 3S and Our Health Society. On August 13, a Supreme Court bench led by Justice J.B. Pardiwala issued an order giving the government two weeks to submit its final decision. Proposed warning labels will display terms like High Fat, High Sugar, High Salt, or Highly Sweetened Beverage. The label text will use a font size one point larger than the nutrition table on the back. Single-ingredient foods such as ghee, edible oil, salt, sugar, jaggery, and honey are proposed to be exempted. Proposed thresholds are based on the Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024. The agency proposed implementing warning labels in two phases. The first phase will start with foods high in two or more specified nutrients before extending to single nutrients. A study in The Lancet estimated that roughly 450 million people in India could be overweight or obese by 2050. Senior Coca-Cola India executive Mili Bhattacharya said during a March 19 meeting that believing a symbol on a label will improve a diet is very simplistic.

The proposed warning labels will display terms like 'High Fat', 'High Sugar', 'High Salt', or 'Highly Sweetened Beverage' in a font size one point larger than the nutrition table on the back of the package.
Single-ingredient foods such as ghee, edible oil, salt, sugar, jaggery, and honey are proposed to be exempted from the front-of-pack warning requirement.

stories.headline: India signs agreement to buy Javelin anti-tank missiles from United States
stories.body: India plans to purchase the Javelin anti-tank guided missile system from the United States. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor announced the purchasing plan. India signed a Letter of Offer and Acceptance with the United States to buy the system through Foreign Military Sales. The proposed sale is valued at $45.7 million. The Javelin is a man-portable missile that uses fire-and-forget technology to track and hit targets automatically after launch. The system has been in full-rate production since 1994 and reached its 50,000th delivery in 2021. India requested to buy 100 FGM-148 Javelin rounds, one fly-to-buy missile, and 25 Javelin Command Launch Units. In November 2025, the US State Department approved a potential $93 million sale involving up to 100 Javelin systems and 216 Excalibur artillery projectiles. Ambassador Gor said that US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth raised the possibility of joint co-production at the May 2026 Shangri-La Dialogue.
